title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
kidExplanation: Slide a window along a string. Inside the window, every letter must be unique. How wide can it get?
plainProblem: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters: Slide a window along a string. Worked example — input: s = "abcabcbb"; expected output: 3. Why: "abc" Interview pattern to name out loud: Sliding window.

thinkingSteps.body: For “Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input s = "abcabcbb" should still produce 3.

thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters in the input string 's', we can use the sliding window approach. We use two pointers, 'left' and 'right', to represent the current window. As we move the 'right' pointer to the right, we expand the window and add characters to a set to keep track of unique characters in the window. If we encounter a repeating character, we move the 'left' pointer to the right to shrink the window until the repeating character is no longer in the window. At each step, we update the maximum length of the window (i.e., the length of the longest substring without repeating characters).

solutions.python:
# Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
# Idea: To find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters in the input string 's', we can use the sliding window approach. We use two pointers, 'left' and 'right', to represent the current window. As we mo…
# Line comments below keep the same logic as the NeetCode 150 repo solution.

class Solution:
    def lengthOfLongestSubstring(self, s: str) -> int:
        left, right = 0, 0
        max_length = 0
        unique_chars = set()

        while right < len(s):
            if s[right] not in unique_chars:
                unique_chars.add(s[right])
                max_length = max(max_length, right - left + 1)
                right += 1
            else:
                unique_chars.remove(s[left])
                left += 1

        return max_length
